taxonomic_note: Accepted taxon; Asian native and introduced/naturalized in North America.
look_here_first: Look at bark and leaf texture together: Chinese elm has distinctive exfoliating mottled tan/orange/gray bark and small glossy, mostly singly serrate leaves; it flowers and fruits in late summer-fall.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Ulmus parvifolia but gives its native range in East Asia, not North America. Flora of North America treats it as introduced and notes that it naturalizes readily in disturbed woods/sites. Texas regional invasive-species material (Quiet Invasion, Houston-Galveston region) treats Chinese elm as invasive and describes natural/spread impacts. The project source pool contains two user observations marked wild, supporting encounter value but not native status.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Native-range status remains FAIL regardless of how commonly the species is encountered. Retention is a separate learner-role recommendation.

best_field_traits: introduced Asian elm, often planted and sometimes naturalized
mature bark exfoliates in irregular plates creating mottled tan, orange, gray and olive patches
leaves small, dark, lustrous/glabrous above, mostly singly serrate
flowers in late summer to early fall
small glabrous samara; seed nearly fills samara
disturbed-site escape/naturalization makes it a useful field comparison
morphology_keys.elm_training: Read leaf texture/asymmetry together with twig wings, bark, reproductive season and samara characters.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Ulmus crassifolia: Both can have small leaves and fall reproduction. Cedar elm has rough hairy leaves, often corky twigs, and hairy samaras; Chinese elm has exfoliating mottled bark, glossy smoother leaves, and glabrous samaras. Ulmus pumila: Siberian elm also has small leaves but lacks Chinese elm's distinctive lacebark exfoliation and has different samara/flowering timing. Ulmus alata: Winged elm has regular corky wings and spring reproduction rather than mottled exfoliating bark and fall reproduction.
